newsitem.title: FINLAND: Human rights to be cornerstone of UN policy -Annan.
newsitem.headline: Human rights to be cornerstone of UN policy -Annan.

text.p: United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Wednesday made a passionate plea for human rights, which he said would become a new cornerstone of U.N. policy.

"I would want to hear music about human rights, about peace, in every concert hall, every popular music hall, in every school," Annan told the Finnish Paasikivi society, a foreign policy discussion forum.
In an effort to ensure that the horrors of the Nazi German Holocaust of World War Two would never be repeated, the U.N. adopted a universal declaration of human rights in 1948.
But U.N. pacts on political, social and economic rights linked to the declaration have not yet been ratified by all member countries, including the United States.

Annan said it was time for the U.N. to play a more active role since human rights abuses had not ended, even though the number of complaints of torture, disappearances and arbitrary detentions had fallen in 1996-97.

A set of reform proposals presented to the U.N. General Assembly in July aimed to give the world organisation's work greater coherence, clarity of focus and efficiency in delivery of services, Annan said.

Part of the far-reaching reform package was an increased emphasis on human rights, with the Geneva-based Centre for Human Rights to be put under outgoing Irish President Mary Robinson, who will become U.N. high commissioner for human rights.

Referring to recent U.N. activities in El Salvador and Guatemala, Annan said the experience had demonstrated the crucial role of human rights in rebuilding trust and fostering a climate of reconciliation.
"Now we must apply the lessons in our present and future work for peace," he said. "New and heightened responsibilities fall on the shoulders of the United Nations.
"The struggle for peace is the struggle for human rights, and against racism, genocide and repression," said Annan.
